| occ6 | Nov-20 ~10:22 | [44715306317](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/44715306317) | Core tests shard 0/4 (PR #2343 dispatch) — verified live: failing step `dart test --coverage (shard 0)` | 7cfcd0b6c0 (`fix/2267-stalehours-alive-keep`) | `test/usage/usage_hygiene_test.dart` | Connection closed before full header |

### Correlation

- **Leg**: 4/6 Core tests (×4 shards), 2/6 PTY/CLI integration (×3 shards) — both on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, both at effective in-suite concurrency 4 (Core has no explicit cap → package default = runner vCPU count; PTY pins `--concurrency=4`).
- **Time of day**: spread 00:28–17:38Z — no busy-hour pattern; the occ1–3 "busy afternoon" read does not hold for occ4–6. It is per-runner self-load, not GH-wide contention.
- **Mechanism**: dart test's loader loopback-ws handshake to a freshly spawned test VM loses the race under subprocess pressure (CLI suites spawn fa subprocesses + loopback servers; 4 concurrent suites on 4 vCPU). Victim file arbitrary, always in the LOAD phase, never an assertion failure (6/6).

## Mitigation: one-shot load-drop retry at the shard step (card candidate (a))

`scripts/load_drop_retry.sh` wraps the `dart test` invocation of BOTH dropping steps (`test-core` shard step, `pty-integration-linux` shard step — exactly the jobs/steps the table names). On a failure carrying BOTH `Failed to load "<path>"` AND a ws-drop signature it re-runs ONLY the dropped file(s), once (the repo's own gh-1026 rerun-only-failed-files discipline).

### Why not the concurrency cap (dispatch preference (a))

- The PTY leg dropped twice AT its explicit `--concurrency=4` (occ1, occ5) — a cap alone demonstrably does not kill this class. Lowering it further collides with the gh-1300 shard-duration budgets (`test_shard_budgets.json`: 420 s/shard, warn at 0.9, **down-only ratchet** — a breach reds the gate AND auto-files an `[ENH]` issue).
- Capping Core (default 4) would tax every green run against the gh-1778 20-min budget sized for the ~14-min degraded-cache worst case, and inflates the per-suite spans feeding the #928 baseline ratchet and the weekly rebalancer.
- The retry heals the whole class at zero green-run cost, at the CI seam where all 6 occurrences landed.

### Safety properties

- **Narrow detection**: requires `Failed to load "<path>"` AND a ws-drop signature on the same line — that prefix is emitted solely by the test loader, so real assertion failures / compile errors never match and stay loud (no rerun).
- **Never rerun blind**: signature without an extractable path → fail as-is.
- **Exactly one rerun**; a still-red rerun fails the shard with the rerun's exit code.
- **Main reporter log never clobbered**: the rerun writes `…retry.json` (evidence only; no consumer reads it) — junit, the #928 duration gate, the gh-1300 budget gate and the rebalancer all keep reading attempt-1 data.
- **Coverage-safe**: the rerun inherits `--coverage=coverage`, so a healed file's hits land in the same `coverage/` dir the gates merge (diff-coverage / 80% ratchet unaffected).
- Quarantine untouched; product test files untouched.

## Validation (this worktree, standalone SDK 3.14.0)

- `test/scripts/load_drop_retry_test.dart` — 7 fixture ACs vs a stubbed runner: green passthrough; heal on both observed signatures; rerun-target precision (only signature-bearing dropped files — a same-run compile-error load failure is excluded); real assertion failure never reruns; ws-signature-without-path never reruns blind; exactly one retry; retry-reporter swap + flag preservation.
- `test/ci_load_drop_retry_guard_test.dart` — YAML-level pins: both shard steps wrapped, `--coverage`/`--file-reporter`/`--concurrency=4` intact, junit steps keep reading the MAIN log, wrapper on disk.
- Sibling guards: `release_hygiene_test.dart` (PTY leg reporting pins) + `ci_core_shard_timeout_guard` + `ci_core_shard_upload_retry_guard` + `ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard` + `ci_pty_aot_seam` + `gate_failed_targets_test` — **96 tests green**.
- **End-to-end smoke**: both edited run blocks extracted VERBATIM from ci.yml (shard-substituted) and executed against a stubbed `dart` that drops a loader file once — attempt 1 runs the full shard, the rerun runs ONLY the dropped file with the retry reporter, exit 0; a drop-always stub fails loudly after exactly one rerun.
- `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` clean on touched files; `bash -n` clean. Targeted tests only per lane policy (no whole-suite run).
- Note: on a healed run, the dropped file's junit durations for that one run live only in the retry log (unconsumed); the weekly rebalancer converges over runs.

Non-goals: the pre-commit fast gate (`ci_fast_gate.sh`) is untouched — 0/6 occurrences there.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# load_drop_retry.sh — one-shot loopback-ws load-drop retry for sharded
+# dart test legs (issue #2331).
+#
+# Family: under CI-leg load the dart test loader's loopback WebSocket
+# (127.0.0.1:…/ws) to a freshly spawned test VM can die mid-handshake —
+#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection closed before full header was
+#   received, uri = http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
+#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection reset by peer, uri=http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
+# The victim file is arbitrary (whatever is loading when the socket dies),
+# never an assertion failure (6/6 occurrences on the card). The shard reds
+# even though every test that ran was green.
+#
+# This wrapper runs the shard's dart test command as given, and on failure
+# that carries BOTH the `Failed to load "<path>"` marker AND a ws-drop
+# signature, re-runs ONLY the dropped file(s) once (the gh-1026
+# rerun-only-failed-files discipline). Real test failures never match the
+# signature and stay loud — nothing is rerun blind, nothing is masked.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   scripts/load_drop_retry.sh <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> "<targets>"
+#
+#   <main-log>   the path of the caller's own --file-reporter=json:<main-log>
+#                (passed as part of <cmd...>) that junit/duration consumers
+#                read — attempt-1 evidence is never clobbered; also names
+#                the <main-log>.console capture;
+#   <retry-log>  where the rerun's reporter writes (kept separate so the
+#                main log is never overwritten);
+#   <cmd...>     the full dart test invocation INCLUDING its own
+#                --file-reporter flag; the FINAL argument is the quoted,
+#                space-separated target list (word-split here).
+#
+# Exit: 0 when the run (or the single rerun) is green; the failing exit
+# code otherwise. Coverage consumers are safe: the rerun inherits
+# --coverage=coverage, so a healed file's hits land in the same coverage/
+# dir the gate merges.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+usage() {
+  echo "usage: $0 <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> \"<targets>\"" >&2
+  exit 2
+}
+
+[ "$#" -ge 5 ] || usage
+MAIN_LOG=$1
+RETRY_LOG=$2
+[ "${3:-}" = "--" ] || usage
+shift 3
+CMD=("${@:1:$#-1}")       # command + flags (including --file-reporter=…)
+TARGETS="${!#}"           # final arg: quoted, space-separated target list
+[ -n "$TARGETS" ] || usage
+
+CONSOLE="${MAIN_LOG}.console"
+
+# Attempt 1 — the command exactly as the step defines it (its own
+# --file-reporter=json:<main-log> is part of CMD; dart accumulates repeated
+# reporter flags, so the wrapper must not add a second one).
+set +e
+"${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS 2>&1 | tee "$CONSOLE"
+RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
+set -e
+if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# Detection: the ws-drop family signature ONLY. A real assertion failure,
+# compile error, or timeout never pairs `Failed to load "…"` with ws text
+# (that prefix is emitted solely by the test loader) — those exit here,
+# loud.
+if ! grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
+    "$CONSOLE"; then
+  echo "load_drop_retry: failure carries no loopback-ws drop signature — not rerunning" >&2
+  exit "$RC"
+fi
+DROPPED=$(awk '/Failed to load/ && (/Connection closed before full header was received/ || /Connection reset by peer/)' \
+  "$CONSOLE" |
+  sed -E -e 's/.*Failed to load "([^"]+)".*/\1/' -e 't' -e 's/.*Failed to load ([^:"]+):.*/\1/' |
+  sort -u)
+if [ -z "$DROPPED" ]; then
+  echo "load_drop_retry: ws-drop signature present but no dropped file extractable — not rerunning blind" >&2
+  exit "$RC"
+fi
+
+echo "🔁 load-drop retry (#2331): rerunning dropped file(s) ONCE:" >&2
+printf '%s\n' "$DROPPED" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
+
+RETRY_CMD=()
+for arg in "${CMD[@]}"; do
+  case "$arg" in
+    --file-reporter=*) ;;            # rerun writes to RETRY_LOG instead
+    *) RETRY_CMD+=("$arg") ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+set +e
+"${RETRY_CMD[@]}" --file-reporter="json:$RETRY_LOG" $DROPPED 2>&1 | tee -a "$CONSOLE"
+RETRY_RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
+set -e
+
+if [ "$RETRY_RC" -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "✅ load-drop retry: healed — dropped file(s) green on the rerun" >&2
+  exit 0
+fi
+echo "❌ load-drop retry: rerun still red (exit $RETRY_RC) — failing loudly" >&2
+exit "$RETRY_RC"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → keyed providers); `tool/fa-clip/` — native macOS pasteboard helper.

**packages/ + app shells:**

- `packages/fa_ui/` — reusable widgets (incl. trajectory) → `docs/agents/fa-ui.md`; `dap_hub`, `fa_llm`, `fa_llm_mock` → `docs/dap.md`.
- `flutter_app/` — the Flutter app (desktop/mobile/web) → `docs/agents/flutter-app.md`; services one-liner: `docs/agents/services.md`; JS apps: `docs/agents/js-apps.md`; HomeKit/Calendar/CodeMie: `docs/agents/system-integrations.md`.
- `browser_ext/` + `lib/src/browser/` + `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — browser extension + WebSocket bridge → `docs/browser-extension.md`.
- `office_addin/` + FA_HOST=office app host — Office add-in → `docs/outlook-addin.md`.
- `fa_network` — external Go backend bridged via the DAP hub (channel-id caveats: `docs/dap.md` §14).
- `site/`, `scripts/`, `docs/subagents/` — landing page (privacy sync), gates + codegen, subagents master plan → `docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

- analyze + format clean; `dart test` green — **deterministic-only**
  (mock LLM; live models never in the gate; `llm`-tagged files run only in
  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module
  dup < 0.31%; CRAP ratchet: core 12.0, app 30.0 (thresholds only-down);
  ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file; AGENTS.md ceiling (top of this file).
- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

Full gate text: `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`; CI workflows: `docs/ci.md`.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in
`cliOnlySettings`/`appOnlySettings` (`lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`)
with the reason; run `dart test test/parity/`. Host capabilities (issue
#1079): every host-wiring capability declares its 7-host matrix state AT
BIRTH (`on` / `off(reason)` / `transport`) via `wireAgentCore` — `off` is
invisible everywhere; extensions are declared surface, SDK invariants have
no override point. Full rules: `docs/agents/cross-platform-parity.md`.

## Commits and releases

- Commit as `ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (set repo-locally);
  subjects `type(scope): ...`. Release-path automation MUST use the
  fa-release-bot GitHub App token — never a PAT or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Every push to main cuts an annotated tag (`scripts/auto_release.sh`);
  the tag is the single version source (pubspecs stay `0.0.0-dev`);
  releases go DRAFT-first and publish at `release-provenance` only with
  signed SHA256SUMS attached. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only (`## Unreleased`).
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag (first publish of a new
  package is manual); every lockfile is committed and enforced
  (`scripts/check_lockfiles.sh`); TestFlight external-group + store
  pipelines have required repo variables.

Full text: `docs/agents/commits-releases.md`.

## Bench

Bench knobs (agent timeouts, stall/watch, `FA_CONN_DEBUG`, hang replay,
report semantics) → `docs/bench.md` (round-3 knobs: issue #1392).

## Docs index

`docs/README.md` indexes every canonical doc (agents/, memory-churn,
compaction, dap, cubes, redaction, hep, ci, bench, browser-extension,
outlook-addin, …). New docs must be listed there.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# load_drop_retry.sh — one-shot loopback-ws load-drop retry for sharded
# dart test legs (issue #2331).
#
# Family: under CI-leg load the dart test loader's loopback WebSocket
# (127.0.0.1:…/ws) to a freshly spawned test VM can die mid-handshake —
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection closed before full header was
#   received, uri = http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection reset by peer, uri=http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
# The victim file is arbitrary (whatever is loading when the socket dies),
# never an assertion failure (6/6 occurrences on the card). The shard reds
# even though every test that ran was green.
#
# This wrapper runs the shard's dart test command as given, and on failure
# that carries BOTH the `Failed to load "<path>"` marker AND a ws-drop
# signature, re-runs ONLY the dropped file(s) once (the gh-1026
# rerun-only-failed-files discipline). Real test failures never match the
# signature and stay loud — nothing is rerun blind, nothing is masked.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/load_drop_retry.sh <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> "<targets>"
#
#   <main-log>   the path of the caller's own --file-reporter=json:<main-log>
#                (passed as part of <cmd...>) that junit/duration consumers
#                read — attempt-1 evidence is never clobbered; also names
#                the <main-log>.console capture;
#   <retry-log>  where the rerun's reporter writes (kept separate so the
#                main log is never overwritten);
#   <cmd...>     the full dart test invocation INCLUDING its own
#                --file-reporter flag; the FINAL argument is the quoted,
#                space-separated target list (word-split here).
#
# Exit: 0 when the run (or the single rerun) is green; the failing exit
# code otherwise. Coverage consumers are safe: the rerun inherits
# --coverage=coverage, so a healed file's hits land in the same coverage/
# dir the gate merges.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> \"<targets>\"" >&2
  exit 2
}

[ "$#" -ge 5 ] || usage
MAIN_LOG=$1
RETRY_LOG=$2
[ "${3:-}" = "--" ] || usage
shift 3
CMD=("${@:1:$#-1}")       # command + flags (including --file-reporter=…)
TARGETS="${!#}"           # final arg: quoted, space-separated target list
[ -n "$TARGETS" ] || usage

CONSOLE="${MAIN_LOG}.console"

# Attempt 1 — the command exactly as the step defines it (its own
# --file-reporter=json:<main-log> is part of CMD; dart accumulates repeated
# reporter flags, so the wrapper must not add a second one).
set +e
"${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS 2>&1 | tee "$CONSOLE"
RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Detection: the ws-drop family signature ONLY. A real assertion failure,
# compile error, or timeout never pairs `Failed to load "…"` with ws text
# (that prefix is emitted solely by the test loader) — those exit here,
# loud.
if ! grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
    "$CONSOLE"; then
  echo "load_drop_retry: failure carries no loopback-ws drop signature — not rerunning" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Properly merge lcov tracefiles (issue #177): `cat a.info b.info` is NOT a
valid merge — sharded coverage produces multiple SF: blocks for the SAME
source file, and naive concatenation makes downstream tools (CRAP, diff
coverage) see only one block's DA hits (methods covered by another shard
show 0%). This merger unions DA hit counts per (file, line), sums
LH/LF/BRF/BRH, and keeps one SF block per file.

Usage: merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
Pure stdlib.
"""
import argparse
import sys


def merge(paths):
    # file -> {"DA": {line: hits}, "LF": int|None, "LH": int|None,
    #          "BRDA": {(line, block, branch): hits}, "BRF": int, "BRH": int,
    #          "FN": {}, "other": []}
    files = {}
    order = []
    for path in paths:
        cur = None
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for raw in fh:
                line = raw.strip()
                if line.startswith("SF:"):
                    name = line[3:]
                    if name not in files:
                        files[name] = {"DA": {}, "BRDA": {}, "FN": {},
                                       "FNDA": {}, "other": []}
                        order.append(name)
                    cur = files[name]
                elif line.startswith("DA:") and cur is not None:
                    try:
                        ln, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                        ln = int(ln)
                        hits = int(float(hits))
                    except ValueError:
                        continue
                    cur["DA"][ln] = cur["DA"].get(ln, 0) + hits
                elif line.startswith("BRDA:") and cur is not None:
                    parts = line[5:].split(",")
                    if len(parts) >= 4:
                        key = tuple(parts[:3])
                        try:
                            hits = int(parts[3])
                        except ValueError:
                            hits = 0  # '-' = not executed
                        cur["BRDA"][key] = cur["BRDA"].get(key, 0) + hits

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Failed-file extractor for the fast gate's flake budget (gh-1026).

Consumes dart test ``--file-reporter=json:<log>`` output (the same reporter
the CI legs already emit) and prints the suite paths of every failed test,
one per line, sorted and deduped — the exact rerun targets for
``FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES`` (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh, integration-mock stage).

Design notes:
- ``result`` ``failure`` AND ``error`` both count; ``success``/``skip`` do
  not. Hidden tests count too — a suite that fails to load reports its
  failure on a hidden ``loading <path>`` test, and that path is exactly
  what a rerun needs.
- A load failure can arrive without a ``suite`` event for the path; in
  that case the path falls back to the loading test's name (``loading
  <path>``).
- A missing or unparsable log is a CLEAN EMPTY result (exit 0, no
  output): the gate never reruns blind — rerunning everything is the
  2.5-hour lottery this budget exists to avoid. The caller treats empty
  output as "cannot rerun, fail the stage".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys

FAILURE_RESULTS = {"failure", "error"}


def failed_paths(log_path: str) -> set[str]:
    """Suite paths of the failed tests in one dart json file-reporter log."""
    suites: dict[int, str] = {}
    # testID -> (suiteID, name); kept until the matching testDone lands.
    pending: dict[int, tuple[int | None, str]] = {}
    failed: set[str] = set()

    def resolve(suite_id: int | None, name: str) -> str | None:
        if suite_id is not None and suite_id in suites:
            return suites[suite_id]

def quarantine_entry(file: str, test: str, issue_url: str,

        "file": file,
        "test": test,
        "issue": issue_url,
        "since": today,
        "runs": runs,
    }, indent=2)


def list_flake_issues(repo: str, state: str = "open") -> list:
    """Open/closed `flake` issues, listed outright — no `--search`.

    gh-1364: GitHub issue search silently returns [] for an unquoted
    `(#<digits>` title fragment (seven duplicate trackers got minted that
    way, one per hourly run), and a freshly created issue only surfaces
    in search after an indexing lag. The label+state listing has neither
    failure mode; matching happens in Python.
    """
    out = gh("issue", "list", "--repo", repo, "--label", FLAKE_LABEL,
             "--state", state, "--limit", "500",
             "--json", "number,title,url,body")
    return json.loads(out)

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: a healed rerun masks co-occurring real failures — the shard goes green with a genuinely failing test**

The rerun targets ONLY signature-bearing dropped files (`DROPPED`), and when it exits 0 the wrapper exits 0 (lines 100–103), discarding attempt-1's verdict entirely. Any attempt-1 failure that does NOT carry the ws-drop signature — a real assertion failure, or a compile-error load failure — is silently absorbed into a green step. The script's own header says "nothing is rerun blind, nothing is masked", and the PR's safety claim is "real assertion failures / compile errors never match and stay loud" — that holds only for *rerun targeting*, not for the shard verdict.

Both variants verified against this exact wrapper (stub runner, one-shotted in a scratch dir):

1. **Assertion failure + load drop in the same run → exit 0.** Attempt 1 prints `[E] Expected: true` / `Actual: false` / `-1: Some tests failed.` for `test/cli/ok_test.dart` AND `Failed to load "test/cli/dropped_test.dart": Connection closed before full header was received…`; the rerun runs only `dropped_test.dart`, passes, wrapper exits **0**. The failing test never reruns; the shard green-lights a real regression.

2. **Compile-error load failure + ws drop in the same run → exit 0.** Attempt 1 emits `Failed to load "test/a_one_test.dart": Error: Compilation failed` + a ws-dropped `b_two_test.dart`; the rerun targets only `b_two_test.dart` and heals → **0**. AC7's own fixture asserts this exit-0 ("a compile-error load failure is deterministic — never rerun") — precise targeting, but the run should stay red.

Under real CI this fires whenever a load drop (6/2-days frequency per the card) coincides with any genuine failure in the same shard — exactly the state a retry wrapper must never hide: the merge gate green-lights a broken commit, and the only trace is a junit error entry on a green job.

Suggested fix (keeps the one-shot discipline): make the rerun include ALL failed suites, not just signature-bearing drops — `scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$MAIN_LOG"` is the existing gh-1026 tool for exactly this: it parses the main file-reporter json (written even on a red leg), counts `failure` AND `error` results, and resolves load failures via the hidden `Loading <path>` test — so dropped files heal (exit 0 only when attempt 1 had *only* load drops) while real failures rerun and keep the shard red. Keep the ws-signature grep as the narrow gate deciding *whether* to rerun at all; use the json-derived failed-suite list as *what* reruns. (If you prefer keeping AC7's precision, the minimal alternative is: on `RETRY_RC=0`, fail the step anyway if the attempt-1 console/json shows failures outside `DROPPED`.)

All artifacts verify clean. The review is complete — here is the final summary.

---

## PR #2347 Review — `ci(shards): mitigate dart-test loopback ws loader drops under shard load`

**Verdict: 🚨 REQUEST_CHANGES (1 blocking)**

### What I verified as green
- All 11 new tests pass (`test/scripts/load_drop_retry_test.dart` + `test/ci_load_drop_retry_guard_test.dart`), `dart format`/`dart analyze` clean on touched files, `bash -n` clean, wrapper committed with exec bit + shebang.
- The **coverage-safety claim empirically holds**: package:test writes per-suite hitmaps (`coverage/test/<suite>.dart.vm.json`) that *accumulate* across invocations — a healed rerun into the same `coverage/` dir preserves attempt-1 hits and adds the healed file's (verified with a scratch-package experiment).
- junit (`junit_from_dart_json`), the #928 duration gate and the rebalancer all keep reading attempt-1 evidence; `flake_watch` only ingests red runs, so the healed run's junit error entry is harmless noise. Wrapper is called from exactly the two intended ci.yml steps.

### The blocking finding
`scripts/load_drop_retry.sh:100-103` — after the rerun of ONLY the signature-bearing dropped files exits 0, the wrapper exits 0 and **discards attempt-1's verdict entirely**. Two one-shot probes against the exact wrapper confirmed both masking variants: (1) an attempt-1 run carrying a real assertion failure (`[E] Expected: true`, `-1: Some tests failed.`) plus a load drop heals to **exit 0** — the failing test never reruns; (2) a compile-error load failure plus a ws drop also heals to **exit 0** (which AC7's own fixture asserts as the desired exit). This contradicts the script header ("nothing is masked") and the PR's safety claim ("compile errors never match and stay loud") — the claim holds only for rerun *targeting*, not for the shard verdict. Under real CI, any load drop coinciding with a genuine failure green-lights a broken commit. Fix direction: rerun ALL failed suites via the existing gh-1026 tool `scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$MAIN_LOG"` (handles load failures via the hidden `Loading <path>` test), keeping the ws-signature grep as the narrow rerun/no-rerun gate — real failures then rerun and stay red.

Digest (not gated): unquoted `$TARGETS`/`$DROPPED` glob risk (:59/:96), single-reporter-flag assumption (:88), healed-shard junit error-entry noise (:101).

**Artifacts**: `outputs/pr_review.json` · `outputs/pr_review_general.md` · `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md`
